question: In an idealized Schumann packed bed experiment, cold liquid is pumped at a high, constant velocity through a hot porous matrix to evaluate the inter-phase heat transfer coefficient ($h_{sf}$). At a specific monitoring probe inside the bed, sensors register that the solid phase temperature stays at $T_s = 80^\circ\text{C}$ while the fluid moving past it tracks at $T_f = 40^\circ\text{C}$. The volumetric interfacial surface area is $a_{sf} = 2000~\text{m}^2/\text{m}^3$. If the local steady heat transfer rate per unit volume absorbed by the fluid is quantified as $q''' = 4.0 \times 10^5~\text{W/m}^3$, determine the value of $h_{sf}$. Give your answer in $\text{W/(m}^2\cdot\text{K)}$ rounded to 2 decimal places.

answers.feedback: Very close, but slightly low. Double-check your arithmetic and temperature difference $\Delta T = T_s - T_f$.

Check your powers of ten in $q''' = 4.0 \times 10^5$ and $a_{sf} = 2000$—you may be off by a factor of two.
